_meta.purpose: Step 4, Issue 3 — proves the cost/complexity heuristic in src/nl2sql/pipeline/guard.py. Heuristic-FIRST, read off the sqlglot AST: cartesian products (join with no ON/USING and no WHERE), join explosion (> MAX_JOINS), and unbounded SELECT * scans. No EXPLAIN — BIRD is SQLite.
_meta.format: Same (candidate SQL, expected verdict) shape as the other fixtures. The benign 'allow' cases mirror the shape of legitimate BIRD analytical SQL so the budget cannot false-reject a real answer.
_meta.rule: Thresholds are calibrated against the frozen BIRD slice gold (max 2 joins, zero unconstrained joins, zero unbounded SELECT *), so the heuristic only trips pathological queries. Old-style FROM a, b WHERE a.id = b.id joins keep their WHERE and are NOT flagged as cartesian.

cases.description: Comma-joined tables with no WHERE to connect them is a true cross product — every row of one against every row of the other.
cases.sql: SELECT a.id, b.id FROM users a, transactions b

cases.description: An explicit CROSS JOIN with no WHERE is an unconstrained cartesian product.
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM users CROSS JOIN merchants

cases.description: Three comma-joined tables, no predicates — a combinatorial blowup.
cases.sql: SELECT a.id FROM users a, transactions b, merchants c

cases.description: More joins than the complexity budget (calibrated well above the BIRD gold's max of 2). Each join is properly predicated, so only the sheer count trips it.
cases.sql: SELECT u.id FROM users u JOIN a ON a.id = u.id JOIN b ON b.id = a.id JOIN c ON c.id = b.id JOIN d ON d.id = c.id JOIN e ON e.id = d.id

cases.description: SELECT * over a whole table with no WHERE and no LIMIT — a full-table dump (also a data-exfiltration shape).
An old-style comma join WITH a connecting WHERE predicate is a legitimate inner join, not a cartesian product — it must pass.
cases.sql: SELECT a.name, b.amount FROM users a, transactions b WHERE a.id = b.user_id

cases.description: SELECT * with a WHERE filter is bounded — not the runaway scan the rule targets.
SELECT * with a LIMIT is bounded and allowed.
A two-join aggregate is exactly the shape of legitimate BIRD analytical SQL — well under the budget and properly predicated. Must pass untouched.
cases.sql: SELECT u.name, COUNT(t.id) FROM users u JOIN transactions t ON t.user_id = u.id JOIN merchants m ON m.id = t.merchant_id GROUP BY u.name

cases.description: A column projection with no WHERE and no LIMIT (not a star) is a normal answer — the unbounded check targets SELECT *, not every unfiltered query, so this passes (8 of the 50 gold queries have no WHERE).
SELECT * over a derived table whose inner query is filtered is bounded by that subquery — the outer star is not a raw full-table dump and must not be rejected.
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM (SELECT id, amount FROM transactions WHERE amount > 100) z

cases.description: A top-level star with a GROUP BY is aggregated — the grouping bounds cardinality, so it is not an unbounded full-table dump.
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM transactions GROUP BY user_id
